newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia's Orient-Avia cargo volume sharply higher.
newsitem.headline: Russia's Orient-Avia cargo volume sharply higher.

text.p: Private Russian airline Orient-Avia said on Thursday it more than doubled its cargo volume in the first quarter of 1997 to 650 tonnes, up from 260 tonnes for the same period last year.
Company spokeswoman Yevgeniya Semerikova said most Orient-Avia cargo shipments were between Moscow and Russia's Far East.
Orient-Avia operates regular daily service between Moscow and Vladivostok and Petropavlovsk-Kamchatsky on the Kamchatka peninsula.
Semerikova also said the company carried 26,900 passengers between January and March of this year, down from 27,000 passengers during the same period last year.
The company's fleet consists of six aircraft: four Ilyushin-62M long-range jets, one Ilyushin-86 wide-body plane and one Tupolev-134 jet.
Orient-Avia carried 161,000 passengers and 1,560 tonnes of cargo and mail in 1996, up from 95,800 passengers and 860 tonnes of cargo and mail in 1995.
